sentences.text: Aucasaurus was a medium-sized abelisaur that walked on two legs, reaching a total length of seven meters, a height of 2.4 meters, and a weight of approximately 700 kilograms.
Instead of horns, this predator possessed a pair of low ridges located above each eye.
The hand of Aucasaurus was unusual because it possessed four metacarpals, but the first and fourth lacked fingers.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — shows impressions of soft tissue at the level of the pelvic region.
The fused tail vertebrae in Aucasaurus represent the earliest known occurrence of block vertebrae in the non-avian theropod fossil record.
The species name A. garridoi was given in honor of Mr. Alberto Garrido, who discovered the holotype.
The Aucasaurus fossil was found in Campanian sediments of the Río Colorado Subgroup within the Anacleto Formation in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
The new genus was named in 2002 by Rodolfo Coria, Luis Chiappe, and Lowell Dingus in a brief communication.
There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Aucasaurus.

Like its relative, Aucasaurus possessed long and powerful hind limbs, suggesting it was a great runner. Traits in the tail vertebrae suggest significant musculature and rigidity, possibly indicating that Aucasaurus was capable of running fast.
Because Aucasaurus fossils were found near a large sauropod egg nest, researchers believe it preyed on the hatchlings and juveniles there.
Paleontologists speculate that the damaged skull of the type specimen suggests the animal was involved in a fight before it died.
Aucasaurus is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
Aucasaurus belongs to the subgroup Brachyrostra.
Subsequent studies suggest Aucasaurus is more closely related to taxa like Carnotaurus, with some researchers including them in the Carnotaurini.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed Aucasaurus garridoi to Abelisaurus garridoi.
The type species of the genus Aucasaurus is Aucasaurus garridoi.
Aucasaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
The type specimen of Aucasaurus represents a mature individual that was at least eleven years old.
